title: Rav Idi, Attendant of Rav Sheshet
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Bekhorot 31b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bekhorot.31b.9): he stated a teaching of Rav Sheshet without attributing it to him. Rav Sheshet took offense and said, “Whoever stung me—let a scorpion sting him.”[^1]

notes.text: Hyman’s heading calls him סרסיה דרב ששת, “Rav Sheshet’s attendant.” [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Bekhorot.31b.9) explains סרסיה as שמעיה, “his attendant.” This is not the designation סריס, “eunuch.” Rashi interprets the scorpion’s sting here as excommunication; the translation preserves Hyman’s quoted imagery.
